messages:
sam_support: Hey team — AcmeCorp demo just blasted through their per-org qps during the 1pm session. They asked for a short-term bump (about 90m) so the demo can finish without 429s. Ticket #INC-1234. Can we do a temporary allowlist/raise for their keys? cc @maya_platform

maya_platform: What info do we need to process? Our standard is: org_id, affected API keys, requested qps bump, duration, business justification, and a rollback plan. Also will need an approver from infra.

ian_sales: AcmeCorp org: acme-42. Keys: key_abc123, key_def456. Business reason: investor demo scheduled, asking for 90m. They’re committed to dedicated next quarter. Sales will own follow-up.

olivia_sre: From SRE/infra: we can do a per-key temporary burst allowance via the quota service. Proposal: add per-key +200 qps, TTL 2 hours, and enforce a cluster-level safety ceiling (do not exceed 80% GPU host capacity). That prevents single-customer bumps from degrading other tenants.

maya_platform: Sounds reasonable. Two approval checks: platform (me) + infra (olivia) for safety. Also need audit metadata recorded (who requested, who approved, reason, TTL). We should have console visibility (temp raises dashboard) and an automatic rollback job.

quota-bot: Automated check: Request payload missing `requested_by` and `change_id`. Please include before approval. Also: temp raises require two approvers.

sam_support: Adding requested_by=sam_support and change_id=chg-20260318-01. I’ve pasted the ticket in the support system and linked the org.

olivia_sre: Approve from infra side. I’ll create the temporary rule now but will gate it behind host utilization check. Command I’ll run: 
```
POST /internal/admin/quotas/temporary
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "org_id": "acme-42",
  "keys": ["key_abc123","key_def456"],
  "delta_qps": 200,
  "ttl_seconds": 7200,
  "requested_by": "sam_support",
  "change_id": "chg-20260318-01",
  "notes": "Investor demo, sales-owned follow-up. Auto-revoke at TTL. Enforce cluster CPU<80%."
}
```

maya_platform: I approve. Two approvers obtained. @quota-bot can you apply the change and emit an audit event + Slack notice when active? Also add an entry in `temporary_allowlist` with fields: org_id, keys, delta_qps, ttl, requested_by, approvers, change_id, policy_scope (per-key vs per-org), rollback_plan.

quota-bot: Applying change now. Creating audit record. Will post when active.

quota-bot: Change applied: change_id=chg-20260318-01. Keys updated: key_abc123, key_def456. Effective until 1768702434 (TTL 7200s). Audit_id=audit-7781. :white_check_mark:

sam_support: Thanks! Two quick follow-ups: 1) Can we route these requests to lower-priority dedicated pool so we avoid impacting critical customers? 2) Can console show a visible flag for active temp raises so support and sales see it?

olivia_sre: For routing: yes, we can tag policy=temporary-burst and smart-router will prefer non-critical pools. I'll set the route tag in the quota change metadata. About console: we currently have a hidden metering metric, but not a user-facing card. We should add `temp_quota_raises` metric and a per-org timeline in Console. I’ll file a small product ticket.

maya_platform: Agreed — product should make the temporary raise visible with TTL countdown and audit link. Also add a telemetry tag `temp_raise=true` to all tokens so we can filter latency/cost impact by raised traffic.

ian_sales: If this becomes a common ask for demos, can we formalize a one-click flow in Console for support requests, which auto-populates the change_id and required fields and kicks off approvals? Sales would love that.

maya_platform: Good idea. Please add to roadmap as small UX. For now we’ll follow manual flow but capture learnings.

olivia_sre: Note for ops: don’t escalate per-org global capacity. We implemented per-key only. If Acme tries to spin up many keys, we’ll still cap at org-level baseline. This prevents wholesale avoidance of org quotas.

sam_support: I’ve informed the customer it’s granted and will monitor. Also added SRE on-call to watch for increased errors.

maya_platform: Closing checklist for this thread: 1) record audit link in ticket 2) console entry + telemetry task created 3) rollback TTL set (auto) 4) routing tag set to temporary-burst 5) follow-up sales check-in. I’ll update the support ticket and mark this thread resolved. :thumbsup:

sam_support: Done. Closing from support side. :white_check_mark:

olivia_sre: Leaving a short note for post-mortem in case of unexpected side effects: monitor `host_cpu_percent`, `queue_latency_p50/p95`, and `temp_raise_count` during TTL. If any metric breaches safety thresholds, auto-revoke and notify rotation.

maya_platform: Thanks everyone. Logging this conversation to the platform audit folder.
